ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.8 meters. It is olive-brown with a black-striped yellow vertebral line and a distinct black post-ocular streak. The body features a reticulated pattern of black crossbars.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Coelognathus flavolineatus* by the distinct black-edged yellow stripe running along the top of its body, which fades into a reticulated pattern toward the tail.
ai.habitat: The Yellow-striped Trinket Snake inhabits tropical rainforests, plantations, and forest edges, typically ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Yellow-striped Trinket Snake is primarily diurnal and highly agile, frequently climbing into trees and shrubs to actively hunt for birds and small mammals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Coelognathus flavolineatus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding generally occurs during the warmer months, though specific data for India is sparse.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Yellow-striped Trinket Snake is found in Northeast India, primarily within the tropical forests of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot at low to moderate elevations.
